page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is an ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by the c4a server family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz, with a 1:1 thread-to-core allocation. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 1608 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong memory performance, achieving a top-tier rating in the PassMark memory score and strong results in large-block read and write memory bandwidth tests. CPU-bound tasks show strong performance in single-core and multi-core Geekbench tests, as well as single-threaded and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database operations and text processing also rank in the top 25% tier. Standard operations, such as stress-ng CPU tests, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, perform within the average range.

The instance offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that benefit from dedicated ARM cores and high-speed local NVMe storage. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a balanced profile, though the lack of hardware-accelerated vector extensions represents a tradeoff for legacy x86-optimized software. This server is highly suited for database operations, web serving, text processing, and software compilation tasks that leverage local high-speed storage and multi-threaded ARM architecture.
